publications.title: Smarter regulation means understanding the trade-offs
publications.summary: Regulation inevitably involves choices.Protecting consumers and maintaining confidence in our markets are fundamental to what we do. But rules also have costs. They can affect businesses’ decisions to invest, innovate and compete. Good regulation means recognising those trade-offs and using evidence to decide where intervention will make the biggest difference.That is why economics matters so much to good regulation.At our annual Economics Conference, economists, academics, regulators and industry experts came together to explore how smarter financial regulation can support sustainable growth and innovation. Across the day, speakers challenged us to think carefully about how regulation affects behaviour, markets and investment, and how better evidence can help us make better decisions.Being proportionate about riskA well-functioning financial system cannot be risk-free, nor should we try
